signals.label: Flu — lab-confirmed hospitalizations per 100,000 (RESP-NET, MN catchment)
signals.levelBasis: Compared with the past 3 years of this measure (39th percentile)
signals.note: Weekly laboratory-confirmed influenza-associated hospitalizations per 100,000 residents of Minnesota's Emerging Infections Program catchment area (CDC FluSurv-NET, crude rate). CDC's Minnesota catchment was the 7-county Twin Cities metro through the 2023-24 season and roughly statewide from the 2024-25 season (week ending 2024-10-05), as implied by the published infant rates; rates before and after that week cover different populations. FluSurv-NET did not report in some off-season weeks before 2025-26; those weeks have no point. Only patients who were tested are counted; untested and non-hospitalized illness is not included. CDC publishes rates to one decimal, so 0.0 means under 0.05 per 100,000, not necessarily zero admissions. The newest two weeks are incomplete and are usually revised upward.

signals.label: Influenza A — wastewater viral activity level, Minnesota (median of 23 reporting sites, derived)
signals.levelBasis: CDC NWSS WVAL cut-points (Aug 2026)

attrs.method: median of site WVALs (sites past WVAL start-up)

signals.note: Derived by MN Pulse from CDC NWSS site data: each week's median Wastewater Viral Activity Level across the Minnesota sites reporting Influenza A that week, leaving out sites still in their baseline start-up period (before CDC's WVAL inclusion date). This is similar to CDC's described approach for state levels (median of site WVALs), but CDC's own state value may differ. Weeks with fewer than 3 reporting sites are omitted; 3 sites reported in the first week shown (2023-06-17) and 23 in the latest, so the mix of sites behind the median changes over time. A WVAL of exactly 1 is common (most likely at or below a site's baseline), so the median is 1 whenever most sites report 1 (18 of 23 in the latest week).

signals.label: Flu — estimated Rt (CDC CFA)
signals.levelBasis: CDC CFA category “Growing (>99% chance Rt > 1)”
signals.note: CDC's estimate of the effective reproduction number (Rt) from daily emergency department visits (NSSP). Rt above 1 means infections are likely growing; below 1, likely declining. It shows the direction of spread, not how much illness there is. Each week shows the estimate for its last day (the newest point is the latest model-run date), from the newest weekly model run that estimated that day; if a later run did not estimate a day, the earlier run's published estimate is kept. Recent weeks are nowcast-adjusted and revised weekly. CDC changed methods on 2026-06-01 (EpiNow2 → spatially pooled HGAM). Blank weeks: no CDC run estimated Rt (e.g. too few visits off-season).

primary.levelBasis: Compared with the past 3 years of this measure (49th percentile)

attrs.Retrieved via: PopHIVE GitHub mirror of CMU Delphi Epidata

primary.note: The share of all patient visits to Minnesota ILINet sentinel outpatient providers (clinics, urgent care and some emergency departments) that were for influenza-like illness: a fever of 100°F (37.8°C) or higher plus a cough and/or sore throat. pathogens.headline: Mpox: 3 reported cases in the week ending 2026-09-26 (not enough history to rate the level).

primary.label: Mpox — current-week cases in CDC's weekly table (NNDSS)
primary.note: Provisional counts from CDC's weekly NNDSS tables for Minnesota. Each point is the table's 'current week' cell as CDC first published it: the cases Minnesota had assigned to that MMWR week when the table came out. It is not a count by illness onset and it is never revised. Cases reported later are credited to earlier weeks and are never added back to these points, so the weekly points undercount; the year-to-date total is the better guide. Blank cells are shown as missing, not zero.

signals.label: Measles — current-week cases in CDC's weekly table (NNDSS)
signals.levelBasis: Not enough history to compare
signals.note: Provisional counts from CDC's weekly NNDSS tables for Minnesota. Each point is the table's 'current week' cell as CDC first published it: the cases Minnesota had assigned to that MMWR week when the table came out. It is not a count by illness onset and it is never revised. Cases reported later are credited to earlier weeks and are never added back to these points, so the weekly points undercount; the year-to-date total is the better guide. Blank cells are shown as missing, not zero. Indigenous and imported cases combined.

mapLayers.label: COVID-19 — wastewater activity index
mapLayers.description: CDC Wastewater Viral Activity Level (WVAL): this site’s viral level relative to its own baseline, so WVAL values and categories can be compared across sites (raw viral concentrations cannot). Reported to CDC NWSS by MDH and/or WastewaterSCAN. Most recent weeks are exactly 1, as are most influenza A and RSV site-weeks nationally (fewer for COVID-19): most likely at or below the site’s baseline. A jump from 1 is how the index behaves, not necessarily an error. The first weeks, before CDC included the site in WVAL, are a baseline start-up period and can be extreme.
